info.title: Tronicare Assets Api
info.description: Source-derived HTTP contract for the Python implementation. Includes operational endpoints hidden from runtime OpenAPI. Use the base URL of this process; no production host is embedded.

200.description: Records, or the single record selected by entity_id.

422.description: Invalid path, query, JSON or wire member.

503.description: Required dependency or mutation authority unavailable.

get.description: Requires entity permission read. Supplying entity_id selects one record and changes the response from an array to an object. Ordinary callers are scoped by their organization AND (user OR groups); privileged callers may use the documented filters. The default API runtime supplements Redis method rights with bounded caller-token Users /v1/usersadmin/context checks of current SQL identity, organization, signed role level, memberships and requested method rights. Stale cached actor state fails closed; the separately configured trusted internal credential keeps its explicit service authority. Ordinary asset access requires the caller organization AND an explicit user OR current group assignment. Item GET and item-selected collection GET enforce the same SQL scope; denied PUT and DELETE cannot change state or append mutation audit.

parameters.name: entity_id
parameters.description: Implicit FastAPI parameter: a positive decimal ID up to 9223372036854775807. GET returns that record instead of the list. POST validates this value but still allocates its own new ID.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Missing/empty/zero becomes 50. Legacy list appends before checking the limit, so positive n may return n+1 rows; negative values return at most one. Duplicate parameters are rejected.

parameters.name: idorganization
parameters.description: Optional signed-64-bit filter, applied only to internal or usertypelevel >= 90 callers.

parameters.description: Optional signed-64-bit filter, applied only to internal or usertypelevel >= 90 callers.

parameters.name: idusergroup
parameters.description: Optional signed-64-bit filter, applied only to internal or usertypelevel >= 90 callers.

parameters.name: idhub
parameters.description: Optional signed-64-bit filter, applied only to internal or usertypelevel >= 90 callers.

parameters.name: includeusergroups
parameters.description: Case-insensitive boolean. True uses the principal's groups instead of idusergroup. Privileged callers only.

post.description: Requires entity permission create. Mutations require both configured and database authority; otherwise HTTP 503. JSON object only; duplicate keys and non-finite numbers are rejected. Unknown members are ignored and omitted members retain their values (or defaults on create). The POST identity is allocated by the server; a PUT identity, if supplied, must match the path. The default API runtime supplements Redis method rights with bounded caller-token Users /v1/usersadmin/context checks of current SQL identity, organization, signed role level, memberships and requested method rights. Stale cached actor state fails closed; the separately configured trusted internal credential keeps its explicit service authority. Ordinary asset access requires the caller organization AND an explicit user OR current group assignment. Item GET and item-selected collection GET enforce the same SQL scope; denied PUT and DELETE cannot change state or append mutation audit. One-time-password sessions cannot mutate. Ordinary asset creation targets the caller organization; ordinary updates preserve that organization and require an existing assignment checked within the write transaction. Platform callers retain their method-right-controlled scope.

503.description: Mutations disabled, or required dependency or configured/database write authority unavailable.

post.description: Requires a Token and assets update right (u), including fresh Users actor authorization. One-time-password sessions cannot mutate. Mutations must be enabled and both configured and database write authority must be available. No query parameters are accepted and no request body is required. The write transaction locks the asset row and verifies ordinary callers' existing organization AND (direct user OR current group) grant before testing whether the assignment exists. The configured internal credential and platform level 90 or above bypass those asset filters while retaining method-right checks. Related IDs follow the source association semantics: no target Users record lookup or foreign-key relationship is imposed. Successful changes and their audit record commit atomically; a no-op does not append audit. POST refuses any existing pair.
